topic_brief.title: Legume rotation effects on subsequent crop yield
topic_brief.research_question: Does including a legume in crop rotation increase the yield of the subsequent non-legume crop?
topic_brief.population_description: Field crops grown after a legume pre-crop in rotation experiments
topic_brief.intervention_description: Legume-based crop rotation (legume grown as the preceding crop before the target crop)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Continuous cropping or non-legume rotation (cereal after cereal, fallow, or non-legume break crop)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Subsequent crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is the SUBSEQUENT CROP yield after legume rotation, NOT the legume yield
Control is the same crop grown after a non-legume or in continuous monoculture
Some papers report legume yield AND subsequent crop yield - extract ONLY the subsequent crop
N fertilizer levels may differ between treatments - record exact rates
Multi-year rotation studies: extract each rotation cycle separately
Some papers compare multiple legume species - extract each vs same control
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of the SUBSEQUENT CROP (after legume), NOT the legume yield itself
2. Treatment = crop grown AFTER a legume; Control = crop grown after non-legume or in monoculture
3. Extract EACH crop-year-site combination separately
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n/replicates)
5. Record which legume species was the preceding crop
6. Record the subsequent crop species and N fertilizer rate
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall +20% yield increase; wheat +20%, maize +22%, barley +16%; larger with no N fertilizer (+28%) vs high N (+10%)

topic_brief.outcome_description: Subsequent crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is the SUBSEQUENT CROP yield after legume rotation, NOT the legume yield
Control is the same crop grown after a non-legume or in continuous monoculture

topic_brief.population_description: Field crops grown after a legume pre-crop in rotation experiments
topic_brief.intervention_description: Legume-based crop rotation (legume grown as the preceding crop before the target crop)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Continuous cropping or non-legume rotation (cereal after cereal, fallow, or non-legume break crop)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Subsequent crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is the SUBSEQUENT CROP yield after legume rotation, NOT the legume yield
Control is the same crop grown after a non-legume or in continuous monoculture
Some papers report legume yield AND subsequent crop yield - extract ONLY the subsequent crop
N fertilizer levels may differ between treatments - record exact rates
Multi-year rotation studies: extract each rotation cycle separately
Some papers compare multiple legume species - extract each vs same control
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of the SUBSEQUENT CROP (after legume), NOT the legume yield itself
2. Treatment = crop grown AFTER a legume; Control = crop grown after non-legume or in monoculture
3. Extract EACH crop-year-site combination separately
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n/replicates)
5. Record which legume species was the preceding crop
6. Record the subsequent crop species and N fertilizer rate
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall +20% yield increase; wheat +20%, maize +22%, barley +16%; larger with no N fertilizer (+28%) vs high N (+10%)

topic_brief.title: Legume rotation effects on subsequent crop yield

topic_brief.population_description: Field crops grown after a legume pre-crop in rotation experiments
topic_brief.intervention_description: Legume-based crop rotation (legume grown as the preceding crop before the target crop)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Continuous cropping or non-legume rotation (cereal after cereal, fallow, or non-legume break crop)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Subsequent crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is the SUBSEQUENT CROP yield after legume rotation, NOT the legume yield
Control is the same crop grown after a non-legume or in continuous monoculture
Some papers report legume yield AND subsequent crop yield - extract ONLY the subsequent crop
N fertilizer levels may differ between treatments - record exact rates
Multi-year rotation studies: extract each rotation cycle separately
Some papers compare multiple legume species - extract each vs same control
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of the SUBSEQUENT CROP (after legume), NOT the legume yield itself
2. Treatment = crop grown AFTER a legume; Control = crop grown after non-legume or in monoculture
3. Extract EACH crop-year-site combination separately
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n/replicates)
5. Record which legume species was the preceding crop
6. Record the subsequent crop species and N fertilizer rate
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall +20% yield increase; wheat +20%, maize +22%, barley +16%; larger with no N fertilizer (+28%) vs high N (+10%)

row.authors: Ping Chen, Qing Du, Xiaoming Liu, Li Zhou, Sajad Hussain, Lu Lei, Chun Song, Xiaochun Wang, Weiguo Liu, Feng Yang, Kai Shu, Jiang Liu, Junbo Du, Wenyu Yang, Taiwen Yong
row.treatment_description: Intercropped maize (IM) with soybean, conventional nitrogen (CN, 240 kg N/ha)
row.control_description: Monoculture maize (MM), conventional nitrogen (CN, 240 kg N/ha)
row.notes: Relay strip intercropping (not rotation). CN = 240 kg N/ha total. Year 2014. Intercropped maize yield significantly lower than monoculture at high N. IMPORTANT: This paper studies relay strip INTERCROPPING, not crop ROTATION. Maize and soybean are grown simultaneously in alternating strips with overlapping growth periods. The comparison (IM vs MM) captures legume facilitation effects but is structurally different from sequential rotation. Meta-analyst should decide on inclusion criteria.

topic_brief.intervention_description: Legume-based crop rotation (legume grown as the preceding crop before the target crop)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Continuous cropping or non-legume rotation (cereal after cereal, fallow, or non-legume break crop)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Subsequent crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is the SUBSEQUENT CROP yield after legume rotation, NOT the legume yield
Control is the same crop grown after a non-legume or in continuous monoculture
Some papers report legume yield AND subsequent crop yield - extract ONLY the subsequent crop
N fertilizer levels may differ between treatments - record exact rates
Multi-year rotation studies: extract each rotation cycle separately
Some papers compare multiple legume species - extract each vs same control
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of the SUBSEQUENT CROP (after legume), NOT the legume yield itself
2. Treatment = crop grown AFTER a legume; Control = crop grown after non-legume or in monoculture
3. Extract EACH crop-year-site combination separately
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n/replicates)
5. Record which legume species was the preceding crop
6. Record the subsequent crop species and N fertilizer rate
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall +20% yield increase; wheat +20%, maize +22%, barley +16%; larger with no N fertilizer (+28%) vs high N (+10%)

topic_brief.title: Legume rotation effects on subsequent crop yield
topic_brief.research_question: Does including a legume in crop rotation increase the yield of the subsequent non-legume crop?
topic_brief.population_description: Field crops grown after a legume pre-crop in rotation experiments
topic_brief.intervention_description: Legume-based crop rotation (legume grown as the preceding crop before the target crop)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Continuous cropping or non-legume rotation (cereal after cereal, fallow, or non-legume break crop)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Subsequent crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is the SUBSEQUENT CROP yield after legume rotation, NOT the legume yield
Control is the same crop grown after a non-legume or in continuous monoculture
Some papers report legume yield AND subsequent crop yield - extract ONLY the subsequent crop
N fertilizer levels may differ between treatments - record exact rates
Multi-year rotation studies: extract each rotation cycle separately
Some papers compare multiple legume species - extract each vs same control
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of the SUBSEQUENT CROP (after legume), NOT the legume yield itself
2. Treatment = crop grown AFTER a legume; Control = crop grown after non-legume or in monoculture
3. Extract EACH crop-year-site combination separately
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n/replicates)
5. Record which legume species was the preceding crop
6. Record the subsequent crop species and N fertilizer rate
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall +20% yield increase; wheat +20%, maize +22%, barley +16%; larger with no N fertilizer (+28%) vs high N (+10%)

row.treatment_description: Tibetan barley-wheat rotation, ≥10 years (CW10+)
row.notes: SD values estimated from error bars in Figure 1. Text states CW10+ yield was 17% higher than CC10+; calculated effect from means is 16.8%. This is the strongest rotation benefit, observed in long-term fields. No CR10+ treatment exists in the study. CC10+ has notably higher SD (wider spread) reflecting greater yield variability in long-term continuous cropping. IMPORTANT: Neither wheat nor rape are legumes. This paper studies non-legume rotations (wheat=Poaceae, rape=Brassica) on the Tibetan Plateau. It may have limited relevance for a legume rotation meta-analysis, though it documents rotation benefits for the subsequent barley crop.

row.treatment_description: Wheat after vetch in W-B-V rotation, (W)-B-V phase, 60 kg N/ha
row.notes: Overlapping LSD letters (W-W-W='b', (W)-B-V='ab'): not significantly different. Vetch FAILED in preceding year 2001-2002 (W-B-(V)=0 kg/ha). Despite failure, wheat yield slightly higher after vetch — likely residual effect from earlier successful vetch crop. No numeric LSD/SE/SD values reported.

topic_brief.title: Legume rotation effects on subsequent crop yield
topic_brief.research_question: Does including a legume in crop rotation increase the yield of the subsequent non-legume crop?
topic_brief.population_description: Field crops grown after a legume pre-crop in rotation experiments
topic_brief.intervention_description: Legume-based crop rotation (legume grown as the preceding crop before the target crop)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Continuous cropping or non-legume rotation (cereal after cereal, fallow, or non-legume break crop)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Subsequent crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is the SUBSEQUENT CROP yield after legume rotation, NOT the legume yield
Control is the same crop grown after a non-legume or in continuous monoculture
Some papers report legume yield AND subsequent crop yield - extract ONLY the subsequent crop
N fertilizer levels may differ between treatments - record exact rates
Multi-year rotation studies: extract each rotation cycle separately
Some papers compare multiple legume species - extract each vs same control
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of the SUBSEQUENT CROP (after legume), NOT the legume yield itself
2. Treatment = crop grown AFTER a legume; Control = crop grown after non-legume or in monoculture
3. Extract EACH crop-year-site combination separately
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n/replicates)
5. Record which legume species was the preceding crop
6. Record the subsequent crop species and N fertilizer rate
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall +20% yield increase; wheat +20%, maize +22%, barley +16%; larger with no N fertilizer (+28%) vs high N (+10%)

topic_brief.title: Legume rotation effects on subsequent crop yield
topic_brief.research_question: Does including a legume in crop rotation increase the yield of the subsequent non-legume crop?
topic_brief.population_description: Field crops grown after a legume pre-crop in rotation experiments
topic_brief.intervention_description: Legume-based crop rotation (legume grown as the preceding crop before the target crop)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Continuous cropping or non-legume rotation (cereal after cereal, fallow, or non-legume break crop)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Subsequent crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is the SUBSEQUENT CROP yield after legume rotation, NOT the legume yield
Control is the same crop grown after a non-legume or in continuous monoculture
Some papers report legume yield AND subsequent crop yield - extract ONLY the subsequent crop
N fertilizer levels may differ between treatments - record exact rates
Multi-year rotation studies: extract each rotation cycle separately
Some papers compare multiple legume species - extract each vs same control
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of the SUBSEQUENT CROP (after legume), NOT the legume yield itself
2. Treatment = crop grown AFTER a legume; Control = crop grown after non-legume or in monoculture
3. Extract EACH crop-year-site combination separately
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n/replicates)
5. Record which legume species was the preceding crop
6. Record the subsequent crop species and N fertilizer rate
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall +20% yield increase; wheat +20%, maize +22%, barley +16%; larger with no N fertilizer (+28%) vs high N (+10%)

topic_brief.intervention_description: Legume-based crop rotation (legume grown as the preceding crop before the target crop)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Continuous cropping or non-legume rotation (cereal after cereal, fallow, or non-legume break crop)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Subsequent crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is the SUBSEQUENT CROP yield after legume rotation, NOT the legume yield
Control is the same crop grown after a non-legume or in continuous monoculture
Some papers report legume yield AND subsequent crop yield - extract ONLY the subsequent crop
N fertilizer levels may differ between treatments - record exact rates
Multi-year rotation studies: extract each rotation cycle separately
Some papers compare multiple legume species - extract each vs same control
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of the SUBSEQUENT CROP (after legume), NOT the legume yield itself
2. Treatment = crop grown AFTER a legume; Control = crop grown after non-legume or in monoculture
3. Extract EACH crop-year-site combination separately
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n/replicates)
5. Record which legume species was the preceding crop
6. Record the subsequent crop species and N fertilizer rate
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall +20% yield increase; wheat +20%, maize +22%, barley +16%; larger with no N fertilizer (+28%) vs high N (+10%)

row.authors: K. J. Owen, T. G. Clewett, K. L. Bell, J. P. Thompson
row.treatment_description: Wheat cv. Strzelecki grain yield after soybean (4 cultivars) as Phase 2 summer crop, Phase 1 canaryseed (partially resistant) background
row.control_description: Wheat cv. Strzelecki grain yield after non-legume summer crops (mean of maize, sorghum, sunflower, millet, panicum; reported range 2953-3245 kg/ha, midpoint used), Phase 1 canaryseed background
row.notes: Negative legume effect attenuated by lower nematode pressure (Phase 1 canaryseed is partially resistant). Treatment mean (2614) is exact from text. Phase 1 canaryseed reduced P. thornei from 3150/kg to 683/kg soil (0-90cm), vs Phase 1 wheat which maintained 5265/kg to 3150/kg. Overall yield 35% higher after Phase 1 canaryseed (l.s.d. 72, P=0.05).

row.title: Wheat biomass and yield increased when populations of the root-lesion nematode (Pratylenchus thornei) were reduced through sequential rotation of partially resistant winter and summer crops
row.authors: K. J. Owen, T. G. Clewett, K. L. Bell, J. P. Thompson
row.treatment_description: Wheat cv. Strzelecki grain yield after black gram (2 cultivars) as Phase 2 summer crop, Phase 1 canaryseed (partially resistant) background
row.control_description: Wheat cv. Strzelecki grain yield after non-legume summer crops (mean of maize, sorghum, sunflower, millet, panicum; reported range 2953-3245 kg/ha, midpoint used), Phase 1 canaryseed background
row.notes: Treatment mean (2448) exact from text. Control mean (3099) is midpoint of reported non-legume yield range. Black gram cultivars: Black Pearl, Regur. IMPORTANT CONTEXT: This paper shows NEGATIVE legume rotation effect because the field is heavily infested with P. thornei root-lesion nematode. Legumes (soybean, mungbean, black gram) are susceptible hosts that multiply nematode populations, whereas non-legume crops (especially millets, panicum, sorghum) are partially resistant and suppress nematodes. The typical N-fixation benefit of legumes is overwhelmed by the nematode damage pathway. From regression analysis, yield loss was 62% at maximum nematode density (8099 P. thornei/kg soil at 0-90cm). Study location: Formartin, Queensland (27.46S, 151.43E), 364m elevation, Black Vertosol, rainfed, 2000-2003.

moderators.mod_nematode_context: P. thornei infested field; lower nematode pressure due to resistant Phase 1 crop

row.title: Ecoinformatics Reveals Effects of Crop Rotational Histories on Cotton Yield
row.authors: Meisner MH, Rosenheim JA
row.outcome: Cotton lint yield difference from cotton-after-cotton baseline
row.treatment_description: Cotton yield after garbanzo beans (chickpea) rotation
row.notes: Ecoinformatics observational study using hierarchical Bayesian model (Model 1) on 1240 commercial field-year records (566 fields, 1997-2008). No raw treatment/control means reported; only posterior mean yield difference vs cotton-after-cotton baseline from Figure 1A. Garbanzo beans posterior mean difference estimated ~-10 kg/ha with wide 95% HPDI spanning 0 (approximately -200 to +180 kg/ha). Effect not statistically significant (HPDI overlaps 0). Model controlled for field (random), year (random), cotton species (fixed), and surrounding crops (fixed). Cannot extract absolute yield means. Approximate overall cotton yield ~1700 kg/ha implied from Model 4 results.

row.authors: Meisner MH, Rosenheim JA
row.outcome: Cotton lint yield difference from cotton-after-cotton baseline
row.treatment_description: Cotton yield after alfalfa rotation
row.notes: Ecoinformatics observational study using hierarchical Bayesian model (Model 1). Alfalfa posterior mean yield difference estimated ~-55 kg/ha from Figure 1A, with 95% HPDI approximately (-175, +65 kg/ha) — overlaps 0, not statistically significant. Text notes alfalfa is a preferred host for L. hesperus pest, which may explain slight negative yield association. However, alfalfa is also a nitrogen-fixing legume that should benefit subsequent crops. No raw means available; all values are model-estimated posterior mean differences. Posterior probability of negative effect ~80% based on figure. Model uses 1240 field-year records across 566 fields.

topic_brief.intervention_description: Legume-based crop rotation (legume grown as the preceding crop before the target crop)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Continuous cropping or non-legume rotation (cereal after cereal, fallow, or non-legume break crop)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Subsequent crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is the SUBSEQUENT CROP yield after legume rotation, NOT the legume yield
Control is the same crop grown after a non-legume or in continuous monoculture
Some papers report legume yield AND subsequent crop yield - extract ONLY the subsequent crop
N fertilizer levels may differ between treatments - record exact rates
Multi-year rotation studies: extract each rotation cycle separately
Some papers compare multiple legume species - extract each vs same control
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of the SUBSEQUENT CROP (after legume), NOT the legume yield itself
2. Treatment = crop grown AFTER a legume; Control = crop grown after non-legume or in monoculture
3. Extract EACH crop-year-site combination separately
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n/replicates)
5. Record which legume species was the preceding crop
6. Record the subsequent crop species and N fertilizer rate
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall +20% yield increase; wheat +20%, maize +22%, barley +16%; larger with no N fertilizer (+28%) vs high N (+10%)

topic_brief.research_question: Does including a legume in crop rotation increase the yield of the subsequent non-legume crop?
topic_brief.population_description: Field crops grown after a legume pre-crop in rotation experiments
topic_brief.intervention_description: Legume-based crop rotation (legume grown as the preceding crop before the target crop)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Continuous cropping or non-legume rotation (cereal after cereal, fallow, or non-legume break crop)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Subsequent crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is the SUBSEQUENT CROP yield after legume rotation, NOT the legume yield
Control is the same crop grown after a non-legume or in continuous monoculture
Some papers report legume yield AND subsequent crop yield - extract ONLY the subsequent crop
N fertilizer levels may differ between treatments - record exact rates
Multi-year rotation studies: extract each rotation cycle separately
Some papers compare multiple legume species - extract each vs same control
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of the SUBSEQUENT CROP (after legume), NOT the legume yield itself
2. Treatment = crop grown AFTER a legume; Control = crop grown after non-legume or in monoculture
3. Extract EACH crop-year-site combination separately
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n/replicates)
5. Record which legume species was the preceding crop
6. Record the subsequent crop species and N fertilizer rate
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall +20% yield increase; wheat +20%, maize +22%, barley +16%; larger with no N fertilizer (+28%) vs high N (+10%)

topic_brief.title: Legume rotation effects on subsequent crop yield
topic_brief.research_question: Does including a legume in crop rotation increase the yield of the subsequent non-legume crop?
topic_brief.population_description: Field crops grown after a legume pre-crop in rotation experiments
topic_brief.intervention_description: Legume-based crop rotation (legume grown as the preceding crop before the target crop)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Continuous cropping or non-legume rotation (cereal after cereal, fallow, or non-legume break crop)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Subsequent crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is the SUBSEQUENT CROP yield after legume rotation, NOT the legume yield
Control is the same crop grown after a non-legume or in continuous monoculture
Some papers report legume yield AND subsequent crop yield - extract ONLY the subsequent crop
N fertilizer levels may differ between treatments - record exact rates
Multi-year rotation studies: extract each rotation cycle separately
Some papers compare multiple legume species - extract each vs same control
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of the SUBSEQUENT CROP (after legume), NOT the legume yield itself
2. Treatment = crop grown AFTER a legume; Control = crop grown after non-legume or in monoculture
3. Extract EACH crop-year-site combination separately
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n/replicates)
5. Record which legume species was the preceding crop
6. Record the subsequent crop species and N fertilizer rate
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall +20% yield increase; wheat +20%, maize +22%, barley +16%; larger with no N fertilizer (+28%) vs high N (+10%)

topic_brief.comparator_description: Continuous cropping or non-legume rotation (cereal after cereal, fallow, or non-legume break crop)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Subsequent crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is the SUBSEQUENT CROP yield after legume rotation, NOT the legume yield
Control is the same crop grown after a non-legume or in continuous monoculture
Some papers report legume yield AND subsequent crop yield - extract ONLY the subsequent crop
N fertilizer levels may differ between treatments - record exact rates
Multi-year rotation studies: extract each rotation cycle separately
Some papers compare multiple legume species - extract each vs same control
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of the SUBSEQUENT CROP (after legume), NOT the legume yield itself
2. Treatment = crop grown AFTER a legume; Control = crop grown after non-legume or in monoculture
3. Extract EACH crop-year-site combination separately
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n/replicates)
5. Record which legume species was the preceding crop
6. Record the subsequent crop species and N fertilizer rate
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall +20% yield increase; wheat +20%, maize +22%, barley +16%; larger with no N fertilizer (+28%) vs high N (+10%)

topic_brief.intervention_description: Legume-based crop rotation (legume grown as the preceding crop before the target crop)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Continuous cropping or non-legume rotation (cereal after cereal, fallow, or non-legume break crop)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Subsequent crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is the SUBSEQUENT CROP yield after legume rotation, NOT the legume yield
Control is the same crop grown after a non-legume or in continuous monoculture
Some papers report legume yield AND subsequent crop yield - extract ONLY the subsequent crop
N fertilizer levels may differ between treatments - record exact rates
Multi-year rotation studies: extract each rotation cycle separately
Some papers compare multiple legume species - extract each vs same control
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of the SUBSEQUENT CROP (after legume), NOT the legume yield itself
2. Treatment = crop grown AFTER a legume; Control = crop grown after non-legume or in monoculture
3. Extract EACH crop-year-site combination separately
4. Get variance (SE/SD/LSD) and sample size (n/replicates)
5. Record which legume species was the preceding crop
6. Record the subsequent crop species and N fertilizer rate
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall +20% yield increase; wheat +20%, maize +22%, barley +16%; larger with no N fertilizer (+28%) vs high N (+10%)
